Fig. 1. The proposed RDI-Pred framework is specifically designed for emergency and high-risk driving scenarios. It consists of three core 
components: a Risk-Aware Exteroceptive Cue Encoder (RSCE), a Multi-Scale Dynamic Encoder (MSDE), and an Intention Recognition Auxiliary 
Task. The entire framework is trained in an end-to-end manner, jointly optimizing three types of loss functions: trajectory prediction loss 𝐿𝑡𝑟𝑎𝑗, 
dense future prediction loss 𝐿𝑑𝑒𝑛𝑠𝑒, and intention recognition loss 𝐿𝑐𝑢𝑡−𝑖𝑛.

Fig. 2. The architecture of the Risk-Aware Exteroceptive Cue Encoder. It employs a two-layer GRU for temporal modeling of exteroceptive 
cues, introduces a Prior-Enhanced Risk-Aware Attention to adaptively emphasize critical risk moments, and constructs a Tri-Agent Interaction 
Micrograph to represent structured interactions among the Ego, TV, and CIPV.

Fig. 3. Framework of the proposed multi-scale dynamic encoder. The kinematic observation sequence is divided into short-, mid-, and long-term 
branches for hierarchical temporal modeling. Each branch extracts dynamics under different temporal resolutions (1D-CNN, BiGRU, BiLSTM), 
which are concatenated and processed by multi-head attention to form dynamic features.

Fig. 4. Visual comparison between MTR and RDI-Pred across three scenarios: (a) passive lane change under right-turn-lane congestion, (b) 
accelerated weaving in sparse traffic, and (c) aggressive lane change in dense traffic. Row 1: real scenes; Row 2: MTR predictions; Row 3: 
RDI-Pred predictions. Blue: ego; green: target; yellow: multimodal predictions; red: ground truth.
